blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
At executive level, Incoterms are no longer paperwork — they are a language for allocating risk between sophisticated parties with very specific views about which risks they can actually manage. The senior procurement leader understands that the choice of Incoterm on a major contract may be worth more than a two per cent price negotiation, because it decides who will be holding the problem when — not if — something unexpected happens.

The questions at this level are strategic. Which party has the better insurance relationships, and what is that worth in expected loss terms? Which one has stronger customs expertise in the destination country? Who has better information about the route's political and weather risks? Each of these shifts the ideal Incoterm choice, sometimes in surprising directions.

Crucially, the answer is not always the same across years. As both parties' capabilities evolve, the optimal Incoterm may shift. Senior teams review these choices periodically, not just at contract renewal, because a frozen Incoterm in a changing world is an invitation to pay twice: once in the contract, and again when the risk materialises.

items.q: According to the text, what does the choice of Incoterm on a major contract essentially decide?
options: Who will be holding the problem when something unexpected happens
The final price of the goods
Which court will hear any dispute
How the goods will be packaged
items.why: "it decides who will be holding the problem when — not if — something unexpected happens."

items.q: Which factor is NOT mentioned as one that shifts the ideal Incoterm choice?
options: The seniority of the negotiating team
Information about political and weather risks
Customs expertise in the destination country
items.why: O texto cita seguro, expertise aduaneira e informação sobre riscos da rota — não a senioridade da equipe.

items.q: The phrase "when — not if — something unexpected happens" suggests that the author sees disruption as…
options: the fault of the weaker party
essentially inevitable over the life of a contract
a remote possibility not worth planning for
items.why: Inferência: trocar "if" por "when" trata o imprevisto como certo, só resta saber quando.

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: Capabilities of both parties change over time.
Once set correctly, an Incoterm rarely needs revisiting.
An Incoterm can be worth more than a small price concession.
Risk allocation is a strategic decision, not paperwork.
items.why: Inferência: o texto argumenta que um Incoterm "congelado" num mundo em mudança faz você pagar duas vezes — logo, precisa ser revisto.

items.q: What does the author mean by "an invitation to pay twice"?
options: You are charged for the goods and for shipping separately
You pay a poor price now and again when the ignored risk materialises
Both parties must pay the same amount
items.why: Inferência: "once in the contract, and again when the risk materialises" — o custo escondido de manter uma alocação desatualizada.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Charlotte revisando os Incoterms da carteira de contratos. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Right, I've now gone through all twenty of the major contracts, and the picture is more interesting than I expected. On paper, most of them look perfectly sensible. The problem is that quite a few were negotiated four or five years ago, and the world underneath them has moved.

Take the two largest sugar contracts into North Africa. Both are still written FOB, which made sense when we had no real customs presence at destination. But we've since built a very capable team on the ground there, and our insurance rates have come down sharply. On today's capabilities, a CIF structure would actually leave more of the margin with us, not less.

The reverse is also true, by the way. There are three contracts where we took on far too much of the route risk simply because that was the convention at the time. Nobody re-examined them. So we've been quietly carrying exposure that the counterparty is now much better placed to manage than we are.

My recommendation is straightforward. We should not treat these terms as fixed until renewal. I'd like us to review the allocation every twelve months, the same way we review credit limits. A frozen Incoterm in a changing market is a cost we simply keep paying without noticing.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: How many major contracts did Charlotte review, and what did she find?
options: Ten; all of them need rewriting immediately
Twenty; most look sensible but several are outdated
Five; the terms are all still optimal
Twenty; none of them require any change
items.why: "all twenty of the major contracts… most of them look perfectly sensible" mas vários foram negociados há anos e o cenário mudou.

items.q: Why does Charlotte argue the North Africa contracts should move from FOB to CIF?
options: Because Czarnikow now has customs capability there and lower insurance rates
Because CIF is simpler to administer
items.why: "we've since built a very capable team on the ground there, and our insurance rates have come down sharply."

items.q: What point is Charlotte making about the three contracts where they took on too much route risk?
options: The counterparty is now better placed to manage that risk
The route is no longer used
items.why: "we've been quietly carrying exposure that the counterparty is now much better placed to manage than we are."

items.q: When Charlotte says "the world underneath them has moved", she most likely means that…
options: the parties' capabilities and conditions have changed since signing
the shipping routes have literally shifted
items.why: Inferência: os termos parecem bons no papel, mas as capacidades e o contexto mudaram desde a assinatura.

items.q: What is the underlying logic of comparing Incoterm reviews to credit-limit reviews?
options: Both are handled by the finance department
Both are risk exposures that should be re-examined on a regular cycle, not left frozen
Both are legally required every year
items.why: Inferência: ela quer que a alocação de risco seja revista periodicamente, como qualquer exposição — não deixada fixa até a renovação.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "The whole negotiation turned on the allocation of risk between the two houses." Here allocation means…
options: the way something is distributed or assigned
the total value of the contract
items.why: Allocation = alocação: como o risco é distribuído/atribuído entre as partes.

items.q: "These are sophisticated counterparties." A sophisticated party is one that is…
items.why: Sophisticated = sofisticado: parte experiente, que domina o assunto.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "A CIF term lets certain costs, which would otherwise be borne by the seller, be quietly ___ onto the buyer."
items.why: To shift = deslocar; os custos são transferidos de uma parte para a outra.

items.q: "We priced the term using an expected loss model." Expected loss refers to…
options: the loss already recorded last quarter
the loss the buyer must pay upfront
the probability-weighted average of potential losses
the maximum possible damage in the worst case
items.why: Expected loss = perda esperada: média de perdas ponderada pela probabilidade.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "A term that was optimal in 2021 can quietly become wrong as both parties' capabilities ___."
items.why: To evolve = evoluir; à medida que as capacidades mudam, o Incoterm ideal se desloca.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em reuniões de contratos e comércio internacional. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "Legal still has to sign off on the revised Incoterm before we send it." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We'll roll out the new allocation policy across the desks over the next quarter." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva.

items.q: "The counterparty pushed back on moving from FOB to CIF." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, discordar — sem necessariamente recusar de vez.

items.q: "We agreed to review the terms annually, but nobody ever followed through." They…
options: failed to carry it to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado — aqui, não cumpriram.

items.q: "Renegotiating a two per cent discount won't move the needle, but reallocating the route risk will." To move the needle means to…
options: take a long time to measure
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, produzir um efeito perceptível.
